To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have developed a new theoretical model to describe the pseudorapidity distribution of charged particles produced by proton and deuteron interactions with nuclei, and have used the model to describe the dependence of the pseudorapidy distribution on collision centrality for d–Au collisions and on nucleonnucleon centre-of-mass energy.

the pseudorapidity density of charged particles produced by the collision of a proton with an emulsion nucleus is proportional to the number of participant nucleons, and that the pseudorapidities of charged particles produced at the midrapidity region in the collisions of a deuteron with a gold nucleus are proportional to the square root of the number of participant protons.

the pseudorapidity distribution of charged particles produced by p(d)A interactions can be simply described using the two-cylinder (2C) model, and that the parameter values of the model depend on the centrality of the collision and on the nucleon-nucleus center-of-mass (c.m.) energy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the pseudorapidity distribution of charged particles produced by p(d)A interactions at high energies.

the dependence of charged particle pseudopidity distributions on centrality in d-Au collisions at the Relativistic Heavy Ion Collider and on nucleon–nucleon center-of mass energy in proton–emulsion collisions.

the dependence of charged particle pseudoprapidity distributions on centraility and energy in pA collisions at high energy, which can be simply described in the framework of our model, and the results are compared with the experimental data.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the model proposed here is an appropriate tool to study charged particle multiplicity distributions in p(d) A collisions.
the pseudorapidity distribution of charged particles produced at the LHC is expected to be similar to the pseudorapidiy distribution of charged particles in the cosmic-ray interactions.

the pseudorapidity distribution of charged particles produced by the interaction of a proton or deuteron beam with a target nucleus is determined by the energy, centrality, and the mass of the target nucleus.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the pseudorapidity distribution of charged particles produced at high energy in nuclear reactions can be simply described in the framework of this model.

the two-cylinder models provide an excellent description of the pseudorapidity distribution of charged particles produced at different centralities and in different interactions over a wide energy range.
the model is a unified description of (pseudo)-rapidity distributions in different reactions and energies.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a unified formula can be obtained to describe the pseudorapidity distribution of the final-state particles produced by the interactions of protons, neutrons, and deuterons with nuclei.
the pseudorapidity distribution of charged particles is independent of the type of projectile, the target nucleus, and the energy of the projectile-nucleus interaction.
the pseudorapidity distribution of charged particles in p(d) A collisions is a function of the number of participant nucleons and the number of wounded nucleons in the target nucleus.
